candidates.statement: When moving to a new neighborhood or a new country, the stakeholder needs to find a new place to live.
context: relocation trigger

evidence_candidates.quote: Mainly when I move to a new neighborhood or to a new country, I need to find a new place.

candidates.statement: Choose the neighborhood or place where the house should be before starting the keyword search, then search with keywords for that area.
candidates.modality: usual practice ('usually I choose ... and then I start searching')
context: search starts from a chosen area

evidence_candidates.quote: So usually I choose a neighborhood or a place where I want to find a house in, and then I start searching by such keywords to find relevant websites for that specific area

candidates.statement: Find out which websites are the most popular or most used in the target area, especially when it is another country.
candidates.modality: stated want ('I want to be familiar')
context: area may be abroad

evidence_candidates.quote: So I want to be familiar with which websites are the most popular or most used there.

candidates.statement: Use listing sites to spot the neighborhoods where options fitting the budget and requirements are clustered.
context: listing sites show available houses and apartments

evidence_candidates.quote: Sometimes there are options that fits my budget and fits my requirements more clustered in specific neighborhoods

candidates.statement: Ask people who live in the country for recommendations about places.
context: people living in the target country

evidence_candidates.quote: is asking people who lives, for example in that country, if they have any recommendation for the places

candidates.statement: Pick a neighborhood close to a fixed destination such as a job or a college.
context: only when a job or college anchors the location

evidence_candidates.quote: if I have a specific job, or if I'm studying at specific college, I will usually pick a neighborhood that's close to that area

candidates.statement: Search listings by size of the place or bedroom counts together with a budget limit.
context: budget limit applies with size

evidence_candidates.quote: So actually, I will search by like the size of the place, or sometimes by bedroom counts. and with also a budget limit.

candidates.statement: After getting many options, filter them down with less important criteria such as amenities, extra features and how good looking the place is.
context: secondary criteria, explicitly called not very important

evidence_candidates.quote: when I get many options, I can start filtering it down, using other non very important criteria, such as if they have, like some amenities, or if they have, like. some extra features, or like how good looking is the place

candidates.statement: After filtering down to several options, contact the people offering the places, which helps narrow the options further.
context: several shortlisted options

evidence_candidates.quote: so usually, after filtering it down into several options, I'll start with the communication process, which will help me also to narrow down my options.

candidates.statement: Let reply speed, completeness of the information provided and the provider's attitude affect the choice among options.
context: some providers reply fast with full information, others do not

evidence_candidates.quote: So after that steps I might start contacting like the people who offer these places, and when I contact them, sometimes like how fast they will reply might affect my choices

candidates.statement: When a provider does not respond, look for the place name, website, URL or phone number and try other communication methods such as email or phone.
context: triggered by no response on the platform

evidence_candidates.quote: So I'll try to communicate with them using other methods like email or phone.

candidates.statement: A missing response is taken as a bad sign that the management is not good.
context: assessment of the provider, no separate action requested

evidence_candidates.quote: It's just a bad sign that the management is not very good, otherwise they won't just skip any type of communication.

candidates.statement: Use these platforms mainly to discover places and proceed with a different type of communication outside the apps.
candidates.modality: usual practice ('I mainly use ... I actually usually proceed')
context: distrust of in-app communication

evidence_candidates.quote: So I mainly use this type of platforms like as a way to discover places. But I actually usually proceed with different type of communication outside of these apps.

candidates.statement: See when the listing information was last updated, because it may be outdated or wrong.
candidates.modality: strong dislike of the current lack ('I hated that')
context: information may be outdated or wrong

evidence_candidates.quote: You don't know when was the time the information was lastly updated. There are no such information. It might be like outdated.

candidates.statement: Have a short communication path instead of a long form whose submission and outcome are unknown.
candidates.modality: stated preference ('you feel like the provider is unreachable')
context: few buttons, long form, unclear submission

evidence_candidates.quote: you will have this long form that you don't know how it will be submitted

candidates.statement: If another familiar way of communication exists, move to that option.
candidates.modality: usual practice ('I usually move to that option')
context: alternative channel available

evidence_candidates.quote: So if I can find another familiar way of communication, I usually move to that option.

candidates.statement: See a small visual timeline of the next steps and of what to expect, including what happens if the attempt fails.
candidates.modality: hedged want ('I might be more comfortable')
context: after finding a place

evidence_candidates.quote: and I can see, like a small visual of the timeline that, like the website, can show me what are the next steps. If I fail, therefore, what should I expect?

candidates.statement: Reach a provider without having to fill all the required personal details (first name, last name, email, mobile, move dates, beds, baths, custom message).
context: all fields are currently required

evidence_candidates.quote: and all of them are required fields, and you still don't know a lot about the one who is providing this house, so it doesn't feel very comfortable to give all this information

candidates.statement: Not write a custom message; just pick the available option the stakeholder likes.
candidates.modality: stated preference ('sometimes you don't want to')
context: when the user only wants to select an existing option

evidence_candidates.quote: Sometimes you don't want to write a custom message. You just want to pick the available option you like.

candidates.statement: Know more about the provider before sharing personal information.
context: little is known about the provider at form time

evidence_candidates.quote: you still don't know a lot about the one who is providing this house, so it doesn't feel very comfortable to give all this information

candidates.statement: Pick a specific apartment from the listed options, e-commerce 'add to cart' style, because housing options are limited and not customised.
context: limited set of existing apartments with given specifications

evidence_candidates.quote: they can just list it with their specification, and I can have something similar to the concept of. Add to cart

candidates.statement: Know what will happen next, including when the provider would respond, before proceeding with an option.
candidates.modality: wish ('I would love like to know')
context: like shipping estimates in e-commerce

evidence_candidates.quote: I would love like to know if I just proceeded with this option, what will happen when they would they respond to me? What will be next?

candidates.statement: Share personal information only after both parties confirm availability and interest.
context: mutual confirmation of availability and interest

evidence_candidates.quote: I think like giving the information could be after confirming the availability from the 2 parties like if they said, this apartment is available, and I said, I'm interested.
before that step I think it's not necessary to give all the information

candidates.statement: The current flow is: visit a site, log in, use a search bar with filters, open details, then either fill the in-site form with unknown response time or find the provider on Google Maps to communicate directly.
context: process summary requested by the interviewer

evidence_candidates.quote: I will have 2 ways either to fill the form inside the website, and I never know when they will respond to me and how efficient is this process. or just to take their location from the map, then try to find more about them, using other websites like Google Map

candidates.statement: Select the search area by drawing a circle on a map, because neighborhood-name search is too specific.
candidates.modality: liked feature ('one of the things that I like')
context: a good option 2 meters away would be missed by name search

evidence_candidates.quote: One of the things that I like is that they provide sometimes a map with a drawing tool where you can just draw a circle around the place you're interested in in the map
because sometimes searching by the neighborhood name will be very specific, like, if there is a very good option just 2 meters away, it will not be considered

candidates.statement: Have reviews from people available, which makes places feel more trusted and keeps the information together.
candidates.modality: liked feature ('another thing that I like')

evidence_candidates.quote: Also, another thing that I like is providing reviews, I think reviews from people, makes. makes places feel more trusted, and could help let you have all the information together.

candidates.statement: Avoid mandatory registration and unknown buttons or extra steps whose outcome is unclear; prefer a site with minimal options and a list of things to do.
candidates.modality: dislike with clear avoidance ('one of the things that I don't like')
context: unknown process leads to leaving the site

evidence_candidates.quote: one of the things that I don't like is actually these extra steps like requiring you to register in the website. And then you have, like, multiple, unknown, like multiple buttons that you don't know. What would they proceed you to?
this type of long, unknown process makes me just skip the website and look for a website with like minimal options and and list things to do.

candidates.statement: Be able to find the items saved through the favorites button afterwards, since there is no bookmark or saved section in the menu.
candidates.modality: expectation of a normal user ('I assume as a normal user')
context: favorites button exists but the saved place is not findable

evidence_candidates.quote: there is a button called favorites. It should like, I assume as a normal user that if I click on favorites it should save the thing I'm looking for. But actually, I can't find where where it's saving it.

candidates.statement: Not be required to register just to do research on the site.
context: registration before any search

evidence_candidates.quote: And also another thing is that when they require you to register just to do a research, so these things throws me off of the of the website.

candidates.statement: Compare three or four liked options on a single page with the main features side by side.
context: 3 or 4 options at a time

evidence_candidates.quote: I wish, if there is an option for comparison, like, sometimes I like 3 or 4 options like, I want to collect them all in in like a single page. So I can look in the main features at the same time.

candidates.statement: Put the favorites entry in the nav bar or at least the first level of the menu.
context: saved items must be reachable in one step

evidence_candidates.quote: It should be like on the nav bar, or at least at the menu, at the like 1st level of the menu.

candidates.statement: Make registration optional (for saving information and autofill) instead of required, since communicating with a provider does not need an account.
context: no need for personalisation in this process

evidence_candidates.quote: Maybe he could. It could be optional thing like if you want your information saved and to be filled directly you can register. But it should not be required.

candidates.statement: Start searching and see the whole functionality directly, without logging in.
context: instead of logging in

evidence_candidates.quote: Just start searching and seeing the whole functionality directly.

candidates.statement: Search the information wanted conveniently, without steps the stakeholder does not believe are beneficial.
candidates.modality: stated primary goal ('your primary goal ... It's like')
context: purpose behind skipping login

evidence_candidates.quote: It's like to be more convenient just to search the information you want without having steps that you don't believe it's beneficial.

candidates.statement: Filter by price range, beds and baths, home type, and extra criteria such as move-in date, pets and utilities.
context: filters offered after the location is set

evidence_candidates.quote: You can filter by price range. you can filter by the number of beds and baths you can also filter by the home type whether you want a house, an apartment.
and also you can filter by extra criteria, like the move-in date, or any other things that you want, like allowing pets, for example, having utilities, and so on.

candidates.statement: Keep the filters optional instead of forcing the user to fill everything, because the user may be unsure what they want.
context: uncertain requirements at search time

evidence_candidates.quote: I like that. The filters are optional. They don't enforce you to enter everything, because sometimes you're not very assured about what do you want

candidates.statement: Avoid missing options whose attributes the provider did not specify when filtering by such an attribute.
context: owner may allow pets without stating it

evidence_candidates.quote: What if I filter by some criteria, and then I lost all the options where the owners didn't specify.
because sometimes I have this fear that maybe I filtered by something, and I missed options that were not entered appropriately.

candidates.statement: Add a checkbox such as 'include options that didn't determine' inside an attribute filter like pet policy.
context: checkbox in the pet policy dropdown

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe if there is like a check box called include, for example, like the options that didn't determine, or something like that.

candidates.statement: With the checkbox ticked show both allowed and unspecified listings; without it show only listings that specify they allow.
context: depends on the checkbox state

evidence_candidates.quote: The one who allowed and the one who didn't specify, and if I didn't click on the checkbox, I will have the ones who only specify that they allow.

candidates.statement: Get an overview of the available options, price ranges, reviews and locations, especially when moving to another country.
candidates.modality: stated benefit ('it will help me to get information')
context: information not obtainable without such websites

evidence_candidates.quote: especially when I'm moving to another country. So I want to be able to know what are the options? And what are the price ranges, and so on.

So these types of filters, and also these types of websites will collect a lot of options together will give me an overview about the price ranges about the available options, and to see the reviews, to see the locations.

candidates.statement: See when the listing was last updated in order to be assured that the information is accurate.
context: feeling that the information may not be up to date

evidence_candidates.quote: Also, another thing that I would really love is to have to be able to see when it was last updated.

candidates.statement: Have website rules that enforce owners to photograph properties in a specific format (sunlight, specific angles), so that users trust the site more.
context: photos currently vary in quality and can be misleading

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe if the website has some sort of rules that enforces people who own these properties to take the picture in a specific format, for example, on, for example, sunlight using like specific angles. Maybe this will give people more trust to use a website over another one.

candidates.statement: No information on the details page seems unimportant; the page seems good as it is.
context: no change requested for the information set

evidence_candidates.quote: I can't see, like any information that it's not really important, like It seems good to me, or.

candidates.statement: The details are sufficient apart from the last-updated information.
context: exception: last updated

evidence_candidates.quote: Oh, it feels sufficient. It's only the part where I said about like when it was last updated.

candidates.statement: Be assured that the listing information is up to date.
candidates.modality: stated want ('I just want to be assured')
context: details page otherwise sufficient

evidence_candidates.quote: It just. I just want to be assured that it's it's up to date.

candidates.statement: Have all housing communication with property owners through the website as a single platform, if the process is clear and fast.
candidates.modality: strong preference ('It will be so good')
context: conditional on a clear and fast process

evidence_candidates.quote: it will be very sufficient to communicate with the property owners through these websites. If the process was clear and fast. It will be so good like to have all the communication through a single platform.

candidates.statement: Make the send-message process clear instead of a vague button that leads to a form with an unknown outcome.
context: reason the stakeholder does not communicate on the site

evidence_candidates.quote: You just have a vague button called. Send a message where you will fill a form and never know what will happen next.

candidates.statement: Give the user insight into how the communication process will go, so that the user trusts the feature and keeps the communication on the website.
candidates.modality: proposal ('maybe it's changing something in the ui')
context: trust leads to staying on the site

evidence_candidates.quote: So maybe it's changing something in in the ui to make the user have some insight about, how would the communication process be? This will make him like, trust the feature more, and never try something else, and just keep the communication in in the website.

candidates.statement: Decide on a home within a week or at most a month.
candidates.modality: contextual constraint ('sometimes you want to decide')
context: time pressure on the whole search

evidence_candidates.quote: I think, like finding a home. It's it's not a long process, like, sometimes you want to decide within a week or maximum a month.
